targetText: Current lunar light permission: The shared nativeLunarPresentation helper grants moonLightEligible only when its phase, lunar-altitude, solar-darkness and failed-surface checks permit it. When the helper reports near-new, below-horizon, daylight or surface-unavailable, it withdraws atmospheric moonlight; diagnostics do not override that permission. Calendar-body Earthshine and the stellar cutout are separate. This gate does not establish current V5 surface availability or native optical pixels.

sectionElements.text: Configuration and diagnostics are read from the fragment after #. Append &debugMotion=1 or &motion=full to that same fragment. A query-only ?debugMotion=1 is not read. The six debugOptic force names are halo, sundogs, pillar, anticrep, paraselene and lunarhalo. Corona, earthshine, refraction and the crepuscular ray require controlled physical scene inputs; no dedicated debugOptic switch forces them.
Full-motion override (the normal default respects reduced motion):
Query-only negative control: these flags are not read from before #.

simTime without timeScale freezes the clock-driven scene. Use the real-time recipe above for a 15–60 second motion check. Flag activation alone does not prove visible motion or correct optical pixels.

Lunar force checks require an eligible night Moon. Near-new, below-horizon, daylight and unavailable-surface cases cannot gain moonlight from a diagnostic flag. Retain the physical scene inputs and crops for optics, and the real 15–60 second watch/clip/delta for motion; never use qaState().clouds.hash as motion proof.
